electric-charges-fields.title: Coulomb force in vector form
steps: For charges at position vectors, write separation and its unit vector.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: STATED THEN REWRITTEN: Empirical law, not a first-principles derivation; point charges at rest in vacuum.

electric-charges-fields.title: Superposition of electrostatic forces
steps: Apply Coulomb law separately to every source charge.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Superposition itself is experimentally verified, not proved from Coulomb law alone; NCERT Eq. 1.5.

electric-charges-fields.title: Electric field of a point charge
steps: Divide Coulomb force on a test charge by that charge.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: For an ideal point source and undisturbing test charge; field points inward for Q<0.

electric-charges-fields.title: Field due to several point charges
steps: Find each individual field at observation point P.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Do not add field magnitudes unless collinear; NCERT Eq. 1.10.

electric-charges-fields.title: Electric flux through a plane and curved surface
steps: Project area onto plane normal to field.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: For a closed surface normals point outward; textbook gives limiting sum and mentions integral, not a separate integral derivation.

electric-charges-fields.title: Electric field on dipole axis
steps: At axial distance r from centre on positive-charge side, subtract opposing fields.
Neglect a² against r² for far field.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Far-field form requires r≫a; exact expression given for r>a on positive side. Point-dipole limit exact for r>0.

electric-charges-fields.title: Electric field on dipole equatorial plane
steps: Equal charge-field magnitudes have cancelling transverse components; axial components reinforce opposite p.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Far-field expression requires r≫a; point-dipole limit exact outside origin.

electric-charges-fields.title: Torque on dipole in uniform electric field
steps: Forces ±qE cancel as a net force but form a couple of arm 2a sinθ.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Permanent dipole and spatially uniform E; nonuniform field can exert net force.

electric-charges-fields.title: Field of a continuous volume charge distribution
steps: Replace small volume element by charge ρΔV and apply Coulomb law.
Sum all element fields; infinitesimal limit is an integral.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: NCERT Eq. 1.27 explicitly stops at approximate sum; integral is limiting notation, not evaluated.

electric-charges-fields.title: Flux of central point charge through a sphere
steps: Central point charge gives radial constant field on a concentric sphere.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Illustrates Gauss law only for central charge and spherical surface.

electric-charges-fields.title: Gauss law for an arbitrary closed surface
steps: NCERT states this generalization without proof.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: STATED WITHOUT PROOF: STATED WITHOUT PROOF in NCERT Eq. 1.31; do not claim spherical illustration proves arbitrary shape.

electric-charges-fields.title: Gauss-law field of infinitely long line charge
steps: Choose coaxial cylinder radius r and length L; end flux vanishes by radial symmetry.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Exactly infinite uniform thin wire; central region of a very long wire approximates this.

electric-charges-fields.title: Gauss-law field of infinite plane sheet
steps: Pillbox of face area A has equal flux on both faces; sides contribute zero.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Nonconducting ideal infinite uniformly charged sheet; finite sheet only near middle. Distinguish conductor exterior σ/ε₀.

electric-charges-fields.title: Gauss-law field of uniformly charged thin spherical shell
steps: For r>R choose concentric sphere; total charge q=4πR²σ.
For r<R no charge is enclosed; spherical symmetry still fixes constant radial E on Gaussian sphere.
electric-charges-fields.caveats: Thin uniformly charged shell; one-sided values at surface differ. NCERT Eqs. 1.34–1.35.

potential-capacitance.title: Electrostatic potential difference from work
steps: The external force balances the electric force during quasistatic movement.
W_{R\to P}=\int_R^P\mathbf F_{\rm ext}\cdot d\boldsymbol\ell=-q\int_R^P\mathbf E\cdot d\boldsymbol\ell
Work changes potential energy; divide by test charge.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Potential reference is arbitrary; NCERT says proof of path-independence from Coulomb law is omitted.

potential-capacitance.title: Potential due to a point charge
steps: External force per unit positive test charge opposes radial Coulomb field.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Point charge; holds for either sign Q; NCERT Eqs. 2.5–2.8.

potential-capacitance.title: Potential of an electric dipole
steps: For r≫a use first-order binomial approximation.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Approximate for finite dipole r≫a, exact for ideal point dipole; equatorial potential zero; axis ±p/(4πε₀r²).

potential-capacitance.title: Potential due to charge system and shell
steps: For uniformly charged shell, external potential is point-charge potential; interior E=0 gives constant V matched at R.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Potential sum for point charges; shell result assumes uniform surface charge. Continuous-charge integral mentioned but not performed.

potential-capacitance.title: Equipotentials perpendicular to electric field
steps: A tangential E component would do nonzero work along equipotential, contradicting ΔV=0.
potential-capacitance.caveats: At points where E≠0, field is normal to equipotential surface.

potential-capacitance.title: Relation of electric field and potential
steps: Move unit positive charge a small normal distance δl opposite field; external work equals potential difference.
potential-capacitance.caveats: NCERT Eq. 2.20 explicitly gives E=−δV/δl normal to equipotentials; full vector gradient is equivalent extension, not separately derived there.

potential-capacitance.title: Potential energy of two and three point charges
steps: First charge costs no work from infinity; second costs q₂ times first potential.
Third costs q₃ times potential of first two; add pair energies.
potential-capacitance.caveats: No self-energies; assemble from infinity, electrostatic forces conservative.

potential-capacitance.title: Potential energy of charges in external field
steps: Bring first charge against external potential; bring second against external and first charge.
potential-capacitance.caveats: External potential excludes field produced by charges being assembled; single charge U=qV_ext.

potential-capacitance.title: Potential energy of dipole in uniform external field
steps: Quasistatically rotate against torque pE sinθ.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Uniform external E, permanent dipole; interaction self-energy is independent of θ and dropped.

potential-capacitance.title: Conductor interior, charge location and equipotential
steps: Static mobile charges rearrange until interior E=0.
Gauss law on arbitrary interior volume gives no excess enclosed charge; zero field makes potential constant.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Electrostatic equilibrium only; microscopic ion/electron charge not individually zero. NCERT section 2.9 items 1–4.

potential-capacitance.title: Electric field just outside charged conductor
steps: Use a vanishing-height Gaussian pillbox spanning conductor surface.
Interior field and side flux vanish.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Just outside a conductor in vacuum at electrostatic equilibrium; unlike isolated nonconducting plane E=σ/(2ε₀).

potential-capacitance.title: Electrostatic shielding by empty conducting cavity
steps: NCERT asserts the general cavity result and omits proof.
potential-capacitance.caveats: STATED WITHOUT PROOF: STATED WITHOUT GENERAL PROOF for arbitrary conductor cavity with no charge within; spherical shell special case proved earlier.

potential-capacitance.title: Capacitance proportionality and definition
steps: For fixed conductor geometry and dielectric, linear electrostatic fields scale with deposited plate charge.
Q\mapsto kQ\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E\mapsto kE\quad\Longrightarrow\quad V\mapsto kV
Their ratio therefore defines a geometry-dependent capacitance.
potential-capacitance.caveats: NCERT Eq. 2.38; assumes linear medium, plates carry +Q and −Q. This is a definition argued from proportionality, not an independent field calculation.

potential-capacitance.title: Parallel-plate capacitor in vacuum
steps: Superpose two sheet fields; outside cancels, inside adds.
Uniform field gives voltage; use C=Q/V.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Large plates, d²≪A; neglect fringing; NCERT Eqs. 2.39–2.43.

potential-capacitance.title: Dielectric-filled parallel-plate capacitor
steps: Polarization produces bound surface densities ±σp opposing free-charge field.
Compute reduced V at fixed free charge, then C.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Entire gap filled with homogeneous linear dielectric; K=ε/ε₀>1. P·n=σp on PDF p81 is TAKEN WITHOUT PROOF.

potential-capacitance.title: Polarisation surface charge and electric displacement
steps: NCERT takes the surface bound-charge relation without proof.
For parallel plates define displacement and relate to free surface charge.
In a linear isotropic filled slab D=ε₀KE, giving polarisation coefficient.
potential-capacitance.caveats: STATED WITHOUT PROOF: Bound-charge relation σ_b=P·n is STATED WITHOUT PROOF on PDF p81; NCERT convention P=χ_e E gives χ_e=ε₀(K−1), a dimensional susceptibility, unlike dimensionless convention elsewhere.

potential-capacitance.title: Partial dielectric slab (NCERT worked Example 2.8)
steps: Treat vacuum thickness d−t and dielectric thickness t as successive potential drops.
Divide Q by V; textbook example t=3d/4.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Worked example, not separate numbered section; slab fills plate area and leaves vacuum elsewhere; fixed Q and neglected fringing.

potential-capacitance.title: Series capacitors
steps: Intermediate conductor stays net neutral; each capacitor has charge magnitude Q.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Ideal series wiring, uncharged intermediate conductors initially; NCERT Eqs. 2.55–2.60.

potential-capacitance.title: Parallel capacitors
steps: All capacitors share voltage V; source supplies sum of plate charges.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Ideal parallel wiring; NCERT Eqs. 2.61–2.67.

potential-capacitance.title: Energy stored in a capacitor
steps: At intermediate plate charge q, voltage is q/C; move infinitesimal charge dq.
Integrate from zero charge to Q.
potential-capacitance.caveats: Quasistatic charging with fixed C; energy is not QV.

potential-capacitance.title: Electric-field energy density
steps: For vacuum parallel plates use C=ε₀A/d and Q=ε₀EA.
potential-capacitance.caveats: NCERT derives from vacuum parallel plates then states generality for electrostatic fields; not a proof for arbitrary fields.

current-electricity.title: Charge transported and definition of current
steps: If ΔQ traverses a cross section in time Δt, define mean current, with instantaneous limit.
current-electricity.caveats: STATED THEN REWRITTEN: Definition, not derived from a microscopic model; positive conventional current follows positive charge flow.

current-electricity.title: Resistance proportional to length and inverse area
steps: Join identical slabs end to end: V doubles at same I; split slab lengthwise: I halves at same V.
Combine proportionalities and define material resistivity.
current-electricity.caveats: Uniform ohmic conductor of constant cross section and material; ρ may depend on temperature.

current-electricity.title: Microscopic form of Ohm law from geometry
steps: Use V=IR, R=ρl/A, current density j=I/A, and uniform E=V/l.
current-electricity.caveats: Ohmic isotropic conductor; current density vector parallel to E.

current-electricity.title: Electron drift velocity
steps: Field gives acceleration between collisions; post-collision random velocities average zero.
Average elapsed collision time equals relaxation time τ.
current-electricity.caveats: Electron charge is −e; drift opposite E. Assumes field-independent average relaxation time in elementary model.

current-electricity.title: Current density and conductivity from drift
steps: In time Δt electrons in swept volume A v_d Δt cross section.
Current density uses carrier charge q=−e; substitute drift expression.
current-electricity.caveats: n free electrons per volume; area normal to flow. Model assumes n and τ independent of E.

current-electricity.title: Electron mobility
steps: Define mobility as magnitude of drift per unit field.
current-electricity.caveats: Positive mobility; for this one-carrier model σ=neμ.

current-electricity.title: Linear temperature coefficient of resistivity
steps: NCERT introduces approximate linear dependence from observation over restricted temperature range.
current-electricity.caveats: EMPIRICAL STATED: EMPIRICAL APPROXIMATION, not microscopic derivation; metallic α typically positive; if geometry unchanged R_T=R_0[1+α(T−T₀)].

current-electricity.title: Joule heat and electric power
steps: Charge IΔt drops potential V and loses electric potential energy.
Collision dissipation equals gained electrical energy; divide by time.
current-electricity.caveats: Resistive steady-state heat, not general power formula for arbitrary source or reactive device.

current-electricity.title: Power loss in transmission line
steps: For delivered load power P=VI, line current I=P/V.
Loss in cable resistance R_c is I²R_c.
current-electricity.caveats: At fixed delivered load power; transformer details are not derived in chapter 3.

current-electricity.title: Series resistors
steps: Charge conservation makes current I common; individual voltage drops add.
current-electricity.caveats: Ideal connecting wires and ohmic resistors.

current-electricity.title: Parallel resistors
steps: Every branch sees V, and junction current adds.
current-electricity.caveats: Ideal connecting wires and ohmic resistors; two branches R_eq=R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂).

current-electricity.title: Cell terminal potential and internal resistance
steps: Electrolyte internal drop Ir reduces open-circuit emf ε while discharging.
External resistor obeys V=IR; equate expressions.
current-electricity.caveats: Discharging cell with current exiting positive terminal; charging reverses sign of Ir; emf is open-circuit terminal voltage.

current-electricity.title: Cells in series
steps: Add terminal drops of two cells carrying common current.
current-electricity.caveats: For aiding orientation; opposing cell enters with negative signed emf, but internal resistances still add.

current-electricity.title: Cells in parallel
steps: Common terminal potential V yields I₁=(ε₁−V)/r₁ and I₂=(ε₂−V)/r₂.
current-electricity.caveats: Finite nonzero internal resistances; opposing polarity uses signed emf. Identical cells: ε_eq=ε, r_eq=r/2.

current-electricity.title: Kirchhoff junction and loop rules
steps: No charge accumulates at a junction in steady current.
Potential returns to starting value after tracing any closed loop.
\sum I_{\rm in}=\sum I_{\rm out},\quad\sum_{\rm loop}\Delta V=0
current-electricity.caveats: Rules are justified by charge conservation and single-valued electrostatic potential; choose consistent current/potential signs.

current-electricity.title: Wheatstone bridge balance
steps: At zero galvanometer current, two bridge junctions have same potential; NCERT loops give I₁R₁=I₂R₂ and I₁R₃=I₂R₄.
current-electricity.caveats: NCERT Fig. 3.25 arm assignment: R₁ and R₃ share branch current, R₂ and R₄ share other; valid at balance only.

current-electricity.title: Meter bridge balance
steps: Uniform wire has resistance proportional to segment length l and 100−l (cm).
Insert four arms R,S,R_AD,R_DC into Wheatstone null condition.
current-electricity.caveats: Balance length l measured from end next to unknown R; wire uniform, contact/end resistance neglected.

current-electricity.title: Potentiometer comparison of cell emfs
steps: Uniform wire has constant potential gradient φ; at each null point no current through test cell.
current-electricity.caveats: Same unchanged driving-current/gradient for both measurements; each balance within wire.

current-electricity.title: Potentiometer internal resistance of cell
steps: Open load key measures emf with no current; closed key measures terminal potential under load R.
current-electricity.caveats: Potentiometer gradient constant; null measurement draws no galvanometer current; closed load draws current.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Force on a current-carrying straight conductor
steps: Count charge carriers in a segment of length l and cross-section A.
Sum Lorentz forces and substitute current density.
concise_steps: Count charge carriers in a segment of length l and cross-section A.
Sum Lorentz forces and substitute current density.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: Derived in §4.2.3, Eq. (4.4). B is the external field; l points along conventional current. Lorentz force itself is an experimentally established law, not derived here.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Circular and helical motion of a charge in uniform magnetic field
steps: Magnetic force supplies centripetal force to perpendicular motion.
Use v perpendicular = angular speed times radius.
Parallel velocity is unchanged; compute pitch per revolution.
concise_steps: Magnetic force supplies centripetal force to perpendicular motion.
Use v perpendicular = angular speed times radius.
Parallel velocity is unchanged; compute pitch per revolution.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.3, Eqs. (4.5)–(4.6). Text uses q as positive magnitude; absolute value makes this valid for negative charge. Pure magnetic force does no work.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Velocity selector using crossed fields
steps: For perpendicular crossed fields, electric and magnetic forces oppose.
concise_steps: For perpendicular crossed fields, electric and magnetic forces oppose.
Equate magnitudes for undeflected passage.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.4.1, Eq. (4.7). Fields and selected velocity mutually perpendicular; wrong-direction particles are deflected.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Cyclotron frequency, resonance and maximum kinetic energy
steps: Circular motion fixes angular frequency independently of radius.
Reverse the dee voltage each semicircle; match oscillator frequency.
At extraction radius R find speed and energy.
concise_steps: Circular motion fixes angular frequency independently of radius.
Reverse the dee voltage each semicircle; match oscillator frequency.
At extraction radius R find speed and energy.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.4.2, Eqs. (4.8)–(4.10). Nonrelativistic; accelerating electric field is across the dee gap; K rises by |q|V per crossing. Resonance fails as relativistic mass effects become appreciable.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Biot–Savart law for a current element (stated empirical result)
steps: Current element field has cross-product direction and inverse-square magnitude.
concise_steps: Current element field has cross-product direction and inverse-square magnitude.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.5, Eq. (4.11). Basic empirical law, not derived; integrate vectorially over entire wire for net field. Vacuum and steady current.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Magnetic field on the axis and at the centre of a circular loop
steps: Apply Biot–Savart to a loop element; all elements lie distance sqrt(x²+R²) from axial point.
Transverse components cancel in opposite pairs; project onto axis.
Integrate around circumference; set x=0 for centre.
concise_steps: Apply Biot–Savart to a loop element; all elements lie distance sqrt(x²+R²) from axial point.
Transverse components cancel in opposite pairs; project onto axis.
Integrate around circumference; set x=0 for centre.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.6, Eqs. (4.12)–(4.16). Vacuum, thin steady-current loop; multiply by N for tightly wound N-turn coil. Biot–Savart law itself is stated without proof in §4.5, PDF p. 147.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Ampère circuital law (stated law)
steps: Circulation around a closed path equals permeability times linked signed current.
When B is tangent and constant along contributing length L, reduce integral.
concise_steps: Circulation around a closed path equals permeability times linked signed current.
When B is tangent and constant along contributing length L, reduce integral.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.7, Eq. (4.17). Basic law stated without proof; textbook applies it for steady currents, with right-hand orientation of path and enclosed current.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Magnetic field of an infinitely long straight wire
steps: Choose circular Amperian loop radius r; B is tangent and constant.
concise_steps: Choose circular Amperian loop radius r; B is tangent and constant.
Apply Ampère circuital law.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.7, Eq. (4.18). Infinite thin wire, steady current; Ampère circuital law is introduced as a law, not proved in textbook, PDF p. 151.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Field inside and outside a uniformly current-filled wire
steps: Choose concentric loop; uniform current density gives enclosed fraction for r<a.
Use B(2πr)=μ0 I enclosed, with full I for r≥a.
B(r)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi a^2},&0\leq r<a\\[3pt]\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r},&r\geq a\end{cases}
concise_steps: Choose concentric loop; uniform current density gives enclosed fraction for r<a.
Use B(2πr)=μ0 I enclosed, with full I for r≥a.
moving-charges-magnetism.final_formula: B_{r<a}=\frac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi a^2},\quad B_{r\geq a}=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: Worked Example 4.8, Eqs. (4.19a,b). Uniform current density and very long solid cylindrical conductor.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Magnetic field inside an ideal long solenoid
steps: Use rectangular Amperian loop: outside field negligible, short legs perpendicular.
Count nh enclosed turns each carrying I.
concise_steps: Use rectangular Amperian loop: outside field negligible, short legs perpendicular.
Count nh enclosed turns each carrying I.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.8.1, Eq. (4.20). Ideal long closely wound solenoid, vacuum/air; end/fringe effects ignored.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Field inside an ideal toroid and zero in its hole and exterior
steps: Use concentric circular Amperian paths; hole and exterior have zero net enclosed current.
Within wound core each N turns links the path.
concise_steps: Use concentric circular Amperian paths; hole and exterior have zero net enclosed current.
Within wound core each N turns links the path.
At mean radius put n=N/(2πr).
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.8.2, Eqs. (4.21)–(4.22). Zero exterior assumes ideal closely wound toroid; real helical windings leak field. B varies across core radius for finite thickness.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Force per unit length between two parallel current-carrying wires
steps: Field at second wire caused by first at separation d.
Force on length L of the second wire.
concise_steps: Field at second wire caused by first at separation d.
Force on length L of the second wire.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.9, Eqs. (4.23)–(4.25). Long parallel wires, steady currents in vacuum; co-directed currents attract, opposite directions repel. Historical textbook definition of ampere is not current SI definition.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Torque and magnetic moment of a rectangular current loop
steps: Opposite sides of lengths b experience equal and opposite forces.
Lever arm between forces is a sin θ, where θ is angle between area normal and B.
For N turns define magnetic dipole moment.
concise_steps: Opposite sides of lengths b experience equal and opposite forces.
Lever arm between forces is a sin θ, where θ is angle between area normal and B.
For N turns define magnetic dipole moment.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.10.1, Eqs. (4.26)–(4.30). Uniform field, rigid planar coil; net force zero. Text first derives single rectangular loop, generalises to N turns.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Far axial field of a circular current loop as magnetic dipole
steps: In far field x≫R, substitute magnetic moment m=IπR².
concise_steps: Start with exact axial field.
In far field x≫R, substitute magnetic moment m=IπR².
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.10.2, Eq. (4.31a). Equatorial formula B≈μ0m/(4πx³) is stated by electrostatic-dipole analogy on PDF p. 165, not independently derived there; valid x≫R.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Orbital magnetic moment and Bohr magneton of a revolving electron
steps: Magnitude of circulating conventional current is charge per period.
Multiply by loop area, then identify orbital angular momentum.
Insert Bohr angular momentum for lowest orbit.
concise_steps: Magnitude of circulating conventional current is charge per period.
Multiply by loop area, then identify orbital angular momentum.
Insert Bohr angular momentum for lowest orbit.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.10.3, Eqs. (4.32)–(4.37). Semiclassical orbital model; Bohr quantisation is assumed, not derived. Intrinsic spin moment is distinct, not due to literal electron spinning.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Moving-coil galvanometer deflection and sensitivities
steps: Radial field keeps torque at maximum at every deflection.
Balance with spring restoring torque kφ.
Divide deflection by current or coil voltage V=I R_G.
concise_steps: Radial field keeps torque at maximum at every deflection.
Balance with spring restoring torque kφ.
Divide deflection by current or coil voltage V=I R_G.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.11, Eqs. (4.38)–(4.40). Text uses R for galvanometer coil resistance in voltage sensitivity. Radial B and linear spring assumed; increasing N may increase coil resistance and not voltage sensitivity.

moving-charges-magnetism.title: Galvanometer conversion into ammeter and voltmeter
steps: Connect shunt S parallel to galvanometer; same voltage across each branch.
Connect series resistor R for target voltage V at full-scale galvanometer current.
concise_steps: Connect shunt S parallel to galvanometer; same voltage across each branch.
Connect series resistor R for target voltage V at full-scale galvanometer current.
moving-charges-magnetism.caveats: §4.11, Figs. 4.25–4.26. The circuit arrangements and low/high resistance reasoning are explicitly in textbook; these sizing equations follow directly from elementary circuit laws and are not worked out explicitly there. I_g denotes full-scale galvanometer current.

magnetism-matter.title: Far axial field of finite solenoid and equivalent bar magnet
steps: Treat solenoid length 2l and radius a as circular slices containing n dx turns.
Integrate over x from minus l to plus l; in far field denominator approximately r cubed.
concise_steps: Treat solenoid length 2l and radius a as circular slices containing n dx turns.
Integrate over x from minus l to plus l; in far field denominator approximately r cubed.
Express in total coil moment.
magnetism-matter.caveats: §5.2.2, Eqs. (5.1)–(5.2). Far field r≫l,a. Text does not perform exact finite-solenoid integral. Equivalent bar-magnet field is identified experimentally; magnetic pole-strength approach is explicitly avoided because monopoles do not exist.

magnetism-matter.title: Oscillation period of a magnetic dipole and field measurement
steps: Restoring magnetic torque and rotational dynamics.
Small angle approximation gives simple harmonic motion.
Read off period and solve for magnetic field.
concise_steps: Restoring magnetic torque and rotational dynamics.
Small angle approximation gives simple harmonic motion.
Read off period and solve for magnetic field.
magnetism-matter.caveats: §5.2.3, Eqs. (5.3)–(5.5). J is rotational moment of inertia (PDF symbol fails extraction); small oscillations, uniform B, negligible damping.

magnetism-matter.title: Potential energy and work to rotate a magnetic dipole
steps: Integrate with zero at perpendicular alignment.
Difference between unstable anti-parallel and stable parallel orientation.
concise_steps: External work opposes restoring torque.
Integrate with zero at perpendicular alignment.
Difference between unstable anti-parallel and stable parallel orientation.
magnetism-matter.caveats: §5.2.3, Eq. (5.6) and Example 5.2. Uniform external field; arbitrary additive potential-energy constant set to zero at θ=π/2.

magnetism-matter.title: Earth magnetic field: horizontal and vertical components
steps: Resolve earth field B_E at inclination/dip I to horizontal.
Divide components and recover total magnitude.
concise_steps: Resolve earth field B_E at inclination/dip I to horizontal.
Divide components and recover total magnitude.
magnetism-matter.caveats: §5.4, Eq. (5.10a–c). Geometric resolution, not an independent law. Magnetic declination D is a separate azimuthal angle. Do not confuse dip I with current I.

magnetism-matter.title: Magnetisation, susceptibility and relative permeability relationship
steps: Define moment per material volume and magnetic intensity.
For linear isotropic material substitute M=χH.
concise_steps: Define moment per material volume and magnetic intensity.
For linear isotropic material substitute M=χH.
Identify material parameters.
magnetism-matter.caveats: §5.5, Eqs. (5.11)–(5.19). Algebraic consequence of constitutive definitions, not a microscopic derivation; M=χH assumes linear response. Text states B_m=μ0M without deriving it. Strong ferromagnets can be nonlinear/hysteretic.

magnetism-matter.title: Magnetic Gauss law and absent monopoles (stated result)
steps: Closed magnetic field lines enter and leave each closed surface in equal flux.
concise_steps: Closed magnetic field lines enter and leave each closed surface in equal flux.
magnetism-matter.caveats: §5.3. Stated/illustrated law, not derived mathematically in textbook; include as foundational exam result rather than present as proof.

magnetism-matter.title: Far equatorial field of a bar magnet (stated by dipole analogy)
steps: Bar magnet is equivalent to a distant magnetic dipole; textbook states equatorial vector result by electrostatic-dipole analogy.
Compare magnitudes with axial field derived from solenoid.
concise_steps: Bar magnet is equivalent to a distant magnetic dipole; textbook states equatorial vector result by electrostatic-dipole analogy.
Compare magnitudes with axial field derived from solenoid.
magnetism-matter.caveats: Not independently derived in Chapter 5; §5.2.4 Eqs. (5.7)–(5.8), PDF p. 184. Axial solenoid derivation is PDF pp. 180–181. Far-field dipole approximation r≫magnet size.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Magnetic flux through a nonuniform surface (definition)
steps: For a small surface patch project its area along local magnetic field.
Sum patches; for a planar uniform field recover BA cos θ.
concise_steps: For a small surface patch project its area along local magnetic field.
Sum patches; for a planar uniform field recover BA cos θ.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.3, Eqs. (6.1)–(6.2). Definition rather than independently derived law. Surface orientation determines sign; flux unit weber.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Faraday law for N turns (stated experimental law)
steps: Flux per turn for uniform field and planar loop.
Time variation of flux linkage produces emf; sign is Lenz opposition.
concise_steps: Flux per turn for uniform field and planar loop.
Time variation of flux linkage produces emf; sign is Lenz opposition.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §§6.3–6.4, Eqs. (6.1)–(6.4). Faraday law is empirical, not derived from more primitive laws in this chapter. Flux for nonuniform fields is surface integral. N assumes each turn has same linked flux.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Motional emf from changing flux and from magnetic Lorentz force
steps: For sliding length l and loop width x, flux changes as rod moves.
Alternatively a carrier crossing the rod feels magnetic force and gains work.
concise_steps: For sliding length l and loop width x, flux changes as rod moves.
Alternatively a carrier crossing the rod feels magnetic force and gains work.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.6, Eq. (6.5). Straight rod perpendicular to both v and B, constant uniform field. Text warns Lorentz work argument is heuristic; magnetic force does no work on a charge, external mechanical work supplies energy.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Rotating rod or spoke emf
steps: Speed of a point at radius r along radial rod is ωr.
Integrate from axle to rim; alternatively differentiate sector flux.
concise_steps: Speed of a point at radius r along radial rod is ωr.
Integrate from axle to rim; alternatively differentiate sector flux.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: Worked Examples 6.6–6.7. Uniform axial B, rotation axis through one end; spokes in parallel do not multiply axle-to-rim emf.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Magnetic braking and mechanical power converted to Joule heat
steps: Induced current in sliding rod circuit of resistance R.
Magnetic force opposes rod motion; external force compensates it.
concise_steps: Induced current in sliding rod circuit of resistance R.
Magnetic force opposes rod motion; external force compensates it.
Mechanical and resistive powers agree.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.7, Eqs. (6.7)–(6.8). Text denotes circuit resistance r, here R to avoid confusing radial coordinate; constant speed, negligible rail resistance/friction, neglect self-inductance.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Charge passed through circuit during a flux change
steps: Apply Faraday and Ohm for fixed resistance R.
Integrate current over the flux-change interval.
concise_steps: Apply Faraday and Ohm for fixed resistance R.
Integrate current over the flux-change interval.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.7, PDF p. 220. Constant total resistance; single loop; N identical turns would multiply numerator by N. Charge formula uses absolute flux change only for monotonic change.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Mutual inductance of two long coaxial solenoids and reciprocity
steps: Outer solenoid S2 produces approximately uniform inner field.
For reverse direction, field of S1 is confined to inner cross-section.
concise_steps: Outer solenoid S2 produces approximately uniform inner field.
Divide linkage by I2.
For reverse direction, field of S1 is confined to inner cross-section.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.9.1, Eqs. (6.9)–(6.14). Two long nested coaxial solenoids same length l, r1<r2, neglect edge effects. Equality is shown for this geometry; general reciprocity asserted, not proved. With uniform core multiply by μr.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Mutual inductance of two concentric loops of very different radii
steps: Outer single loop yields nearly uniform field over small inner loop.
Calculate flux and divide by outer current.
concise_steps: Outer single loop yields nearly uniform field over small inner loop.
Calculate flux and divide by outer current.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: Worked Example 6.9. Single-turn coaxial concentric loops with r1≪r2, vacuum; multiply by N1N2 for identical closely wound multicoils.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Mutually induced emf from changing current
steps: Flux linkage through coil 1 due to current in coil 2.
concise_steps: Flux linkage through coil 1 due to current in coil 2.
Differentiate and apply Faraday sign.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.9.1 end. Fixed geometry and time-independent M; textbook derives from its mutual-inductance definition.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Self-induced back emf and self-inductance of long solenoid
steps: Define flux linkage and apply Faraday law.
For long solenoid with n turns per length and cross-section A.
Divide by I; insert core permeability if linear.
concise_steps: Define flux linkage and apply Faraday law.
For long solenoid with n turns per length and cross-section A.
Divide by I; insert core permeability if linear.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.9.2, Eqs. (6.15)–(6.18). Long tightly wound solenoid, negligible fringe field, fixed geometry; core formula assumes constant μr. Minus sign signifies opposition to change, not always negative voltage magnitude.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Energy stored in inductor
steps: Power supplied against back emf while current increases.
Integrate from zero current to I.
concise_steps: Power supplied against back emf while current increases.
Integrate from zero current to I.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.9.2, Eq. (6.19). Constant L; resistance losses excluded when computing stored magnetic energy.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Magnetic energy density from long-solenoid energy
steps: Use solenoid L and B-to-current conversion.
Substitute into inductor energy, then divide by solenoid volume.
concise_steps: Use solenoid L and B-to-current conversion.
Substitute into inductor energy, then divide by solenoid volume.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: Worked Example 6.10, Eq. (6.20). Derived using empty/air-cored solenoid; for a linear magnetic medium energy density is BH/2 rather than universally B²/(2μ0). Text compares vacuum electric density ε0E²/2.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Alternating emf from uniformly rotating coil generator
steps: A turns with normal at θ=ωt to uniform B; flux per turn.
Identify peak emf and rotational frequency.
concise_steps: A turns with normal at θ=ωt to uniform B; flux per turn.
Differentiate N-turn flux linkage.
Identify peak emf and rotational frequency.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.10, Eqs. (6.21)–(6.23). Uniform B and constant ω; coil axis perpendicular to B, initial area normal aligned with B. Instantaneous emf, not rms. Generator converts supplied mechanical energy to electrical energy.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Lenz direction and energy-conservation argument (stated law)
steps: Induced emf polarity opposes the change in linked flux.
Approaching north pole is repelled by induced current; external work can dissipate as heat.
concise_steps: Induced emf polarity opposes the change in linked flux.
Approaching north pole is repelled by induced current; external work can dissipate as heat.
electromagnetic-induction.caveats: §6.5. Qualitative conservation argument, not an independent mathematical proof; opening the circuit removes sustained induced current but not induced emf.
